## Getting set up

- Install [Julia](https://julialang.org/downloads/) (use the latest stable release).
- Install a code editor — [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) with the
  [Julia extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=julialang.language-julia)
  is recommended.
- Install [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and create a [GitHub](https://github.com/)
  account for submitting homeworks.

## Julia

- [Julia documentation](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/)
- [Julia performance tips](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/manual/performance-tips/) — very helpful.
- [QuantEcon (Julia)](https://julia.quantecon.org/) — much of this course borrows from here.

## Computational economics

- [Jesús Fernández-Villaverde's teaching page](https://www.sas.upenn.edu/~jesusfv/teaching.html) — lecture notes on computation and much else.
- Dean Corbae's Computational Economics course — this bootcamp is designed to prepare you for it.
- [Florian Oswald's teaching page](https://floswald.github.io/#teaching) (Julia and R).
- [Gentzkow & Shapiro, *Code and Data for the Social Sciences*](https://web.stanford.edu/~gentzkow/research/CodeAndData.pdf) — best practices for coding and data.

## UW-Madison

- [Social Science Computing Cooperative (SSCC)](https://sscc.wisc.edu/) — computing resources for research.
